candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 38:2 (Esau-Jacob war (38:2)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Judah's sons drew their bows, and shot at Adoram and slew him; and Levi took Reuben aside, and they sent against the men who were on the right and the left, and they slew them' — Jubilees credits Judah and Levi specifically with the battlefield victory over Esau's forces. The Tewahedo Solomonic-dynasty (descending from Judah through David) preserves a memory of the Judah-as-battlefield-leader patriarchal-canonical pattern: the Tewahedo king (nəguś) takes the field with the priest (kǝhnät) accompanying — the Judah-Levi battlefield partnership is the canonical-patriarchal antecedent of the Tewahedo king-and-priest joint-leadership pattern at moments of national crisis.
